headline: An amateur astronomer used AI coding tools to spot a star that may have an undiscovered planet, and NASA's TESS telescope will soon check it.
score_reason: Kept at 5: an interesting but unconfirmed candidate that depends on observations still to come.
importance_line: It shows non-professionals can now run large searches of public space data with AI tools, which could add candidates for astronomers to vet, but the signal could still turn out to be something other than a planet.
summary: Gizmodo reports that Pavel Rabtsevich, a 28-year-old product manager in Spain with no formal astronomy training, used Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex to search public data from NASA's TESS space telescope and found a star, TIC 4206066 about 116 light-years away, whose brightness dips every 3.18 days, a pattern that could mean a planet about 1.4 times Earth's size. It is only a candidate: TESS is due to watch the star from 31 Oct to 26 Nov 2026 to test his published predictions, and a NASA scientist notes the hard part is ruling out false positives such as binary stars.
notes: The 126,000-star figure is Rabtsevich's own; no independent confirmation.
